title: Conditional predictions from a GAM — conditional_values
code: load_mgcv() df <- data_sim("eg1", seed = 2) m1 <- gam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3), data = df, method = "REML")  # predictions conditional on values evenly spaced over x2, all other # variables in model are held at representative values cv <- conditional_values(   m1,   condition = "x2" ) # plot cv |> draw()   # as above but condition on `x1` also. When plotted, `x1` is mapped to the # colour channel, noting that it has been summarised using fivenum() cv <- conditional_values(   m1,   condition = c("x2", "x1") ) # plot cv |> draw()   # can pass `condition` a list, allowing for greater flexibility # For example, here we condition on all four variables in the model, # summarising: #   * `x1` at its five number summary, #   * `x0  at its quartiles #   * `x3` at its mean a d mean +/- sd cv <- conditional_values(   m1,   condition = list("x2", x1 = "fivenum", x0 = "quartile", x3 = "threenum") ) # plot cv |> draw()   # some model terms can be exclude from the conditional predictions using the # `exclude` mechanism of `predict.gam`. Here we exclude the effects of # `s(x0)` and `s(x3)` from the conditional predictions. This, in effect, # treats these smooths as having **0** effect on the conditional predictions # of the response, even though the two smooths conditioned on (`s(x2)` and # `s(x1)`) were estimated given the two excluded smooths were in the model cv <- conditional_values(   m1,   condition = list("x2", x1 = "minmax"),   exclude = c("s(x0)", "s(x3)") ) # plot cv |> draw()   # categorical conditions are also handled df <- data_sim("eg4", seed = 2) m2 <- gam(y ~ fac + s(x2, by = fac) + s(x0), data = df, method = "REML") cv <- conditional_values(   m2,   condition = list("fac", x2 = "fivenum") ) # plot - we see a discrete x axis cv |> draw()   # in this example we condition on `x2` and `fac %in% c(2,3)` cv <- conditional_values(   m2,   condition = list("x2", fac = 2:3) ) # plot - smooths of `x2` for `fac == 2` and `fac == 3` cv |> draw()

title: Model diagnostic support and conventions — diagnostic_support
text: PIT means probability integral transform: fitted cumulative distribution function (CDF) maps observation probability. discrete values, probability randomised corresponding probability mass. Quantile residuals transform PIT values standard-normal scores. posterior predictive check (PPC) compares observed responses simulated data sets also include approximate uncertainty fitted parameters. table applies supported response families described . lm/glm: weighted Gaussian supported response families, fitted dispersion. Quasi families specify response distribution, support PIT/quantile residuals PPCs. gam/bam: ordinary, distributional grouped families, including weighted Gamma, inverse Gaussian, twlss, ordinal ziP distributions. Multivariate-normal PITs check response separately; simulations retain covariance responses. Nominal multinomial models retain traditional residual checks PPCs. PITs require ordering categories. SCAM models support ordinary posterior predictive plots. Scalable posterior predictive plots currently available; use scalable = FALSE. Smoothing-parameter uncertainty currently supported SCAM models; use unconditional = FALSE. gamm/gamm4 direct lme/merMod fits use full predictors. title: Plot smooth and parametric terms from a fitted GAM — draw.gam
code: load_mgcv()  # simulate some data df1 <- data_sim("eg1", n = 400, dist = "normal", scale = 2, seed = 2) # fit GAM m1 <- gam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3), data = df1, method = "REML")  # plot all smooths draw(m1)   # can add partial residuals draw(m1, residuals = TRUE)   df2 <- data_sim("eg2", n = 1000, dist = "normal", scale = 1, seed = 2) m2 <- gam(y ~ s(x, z, k = 40), data = df2, method = "REML") draw(m2, contour = FALSE, n_2d = 50)  draw(m2, surface = "tile", n_2d = 30)   if (requireNamespace("ggcube", quietly = TRUE)) {   draw(m2, surface = "3d", n_2d = 20,     surface_3d = list(yaw = 45, persp = FALSE))   panels <- assemble(m2, surface = "3d", n_2d = 20)   # Replace coordinates to customize a single term; retain the current theme.   panels[[1]] <- panels[[1]] +     ggcube::coord_3d(yaw = -20,       light = ggcube::light(backface_scale = 1))[[1]]   patchwork::wrap_plots(panels) } #> Coordinate system already present. #> i Adding new coordinate system, which will replace the existing one.   # See https://gavinsimpson.github.io/gratia/articles/custom-plotting.html # for more examples and for details on how to modify the theme of all the # plots produced by draw(). To modify all panels, for example to change the # theme, use the & operator

title: Plot smooths of a GAMLSS model estimated by GJRM::gamlss — draw.gamlss
code: if (suppressPackageStartupMessages(require("GJRM", quietly = TRUE))) {   # follow example from ?GJRM::gamlss   load_mgcv()   suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("GJRM"))   set.seed(0)   n <- 100   x1 <- round(runif(n))   x2 <- runif(n)   x3 <- runif(n)   f1 <- function(x) cos(pi * 2 * x) + sin(pi * x)   y1 <- -1.55 + 2 * x1 + f1(x2) + rnorm(n)   dataSim <- data.frame(y1, x1, x2, x3)    eq_mu <- y1 ~ x1 + s(x2)   eq_s <- ~ s(x3, k = 6)   fl <- list(eq_mu, eq_s)   m <- gamlss(fl, data = dataSim)    draw(m) }

code: load_mgcv() dat1 <- data_sim("eg1", n = 400, dist = "normal", scale = 1, seed = 1) ## a single smooth GAM m1 <- gam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3), data = dat1, method = "REML") ## posterior smooths from m1 sm1 <- smooth_samples(m1, n = 15, seed = 23478) ## plot draw(sm1, alpha = 0.7)  ## plot only 5 randomly smapled draws draw(sm1, n_samples = 5, alpha = 0.7)   ## A factor-by smooth example dat2 <- data_sim("eg4", n = 400, dist = "normal", scale = 1, seed = 1) ## a multi-smooth GAM with a factor-by smooth m2 <- gam(y ~ fac + s(x2, by = fac) + s(x0), data = dat2, method = "REML") ## posterior smooths from m1 sm2 <- smooth_samples(m2, n = 15, seed = 23478) ## plot, this time selecting only the factor-by smooth draw(sm2, select = "s(x2)", partial_match = TRUE, alpha = 0.7)   # \donttest{ ## A 2D smooth example dat3 <- data_sim("eg2", n = 400, dist = "normal", scale = 1, seed = 1) ## fit a 2D smooth m3 <- gam(y ~ te(x, z), data = dat3, method = "REML") ## get samples sm3 <- smooth_samples(m3, n = 10) ## plot just 6 of the draws, with contour line overlays draw(sm3, n_samples = 6, contour = TRUE, seed = 42)  # }

title: Effects and diagnostics for glmmTMB models — qq_plot.glmmTMB
code: if (requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly = TRUE)) {   library("mgcv")   set.seed(42)   d <- data.frame(x = runif(150))   d$y <- sin(6 * d$x) + rnorm(150, sd = 0.2)   m <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(y ~ s(x, k = 8), data = d, REML = TRUE)   draw(m)   appraise(m, seed = 42)    # Parametric terms and native random intercepts and slopes   d$z <- rnorm(150)   d$g <- factor(rep(seq_len(10), each = 15))   d$y <- d$y + 0.5 * d$z + rnorm(10)[d$g] + rnorm(10)[d$g] * d$z   mixed <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(y ~ z + s(x, k = 8) + (1 + z | g),     data = d, REML = TRUE)   draw(mixed) # separate QQ panels for intercepts and slopes   draw(mixed, ranef_lines = TRUE) # random contributions only }

code: library("ggplot2") library("patchwork") load_mgcv() df <- data_sim("eg2", n = 2000, dist = "normal", scale = 0.5, seed = 42)  # fit the GAM (note: for execution time reasons, k is set articifially low) m <- gam(y ~ te(x, z, k = c(5, 5)), data = df, method = "REML")  # data slice through te(x,z) holding z == 0.4 ds <- data_slice(m, x = evenly(x, n = 100), z = 0.4)  # evaluate te(x,z) at values of x & z sm <- smooth_estimates(m, select = "te(x,z)", data = ds) |>   add_confint()  # partial derivatives pd_x <- partial_derivatives(m, data = ds, type = "central", focal = "x")  # draw te(x,z) p1 <- draw(m, rug = FALSE) &   geom_hline(yintercept = 0.4, linewidth = 1) p1   # draw te(x,z) along slice cap <- expression(z == 0.4) p2 <- sm |>   ggplot(aes(x = x, y = .estimate)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = .lower_ci, ymax = .upper_ci), alpha = 0.2) +   geom_line() +   labs(     x = "x", y = "Partial effect", title = "te(x,z)",     caption = cap   ) p2   # draw partial derivs p3 <- pd_x |>   draw() +   labs(caption = cap) p3   # draw all three panels p1 + p2 + p3 + plot_layout(ncol = 3)

title: Derivatives on the response scale from an estimated GAM — response_derivatives
code: library("ggplot2") library("patchwork") load_mgcv() df <- data_sim("eg1", dist = "negbin", scale = 0.25, seed = 42)  # fit the GAM (note: for execution time reasons using bam()) m <- bam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3),   data = df, family = nb(), method = "fREML" )  # data slice through data along x2 - all other covariates will be set to # typical values (value closest to median) ds <- data_slice(m, x2 = evenly(x2, n = 100))  # fitted values along x2 fv <- fitted_values(m, data = ds)  # response derivatives - ideally n_sim = >10000 y_d <- response_derivatives(m,   data = ds, type = "central", focal = "x2",   eps = 0.01, seed = 21, n_sim = 1000 )  # draw fitted values along x2 p1 <- fv |>   ggplot(aes(x = x2, y = .fitted)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = .lower_ci, ymax = .upper_ci, y = NULL),     alpha = 0.2   ) +   geom_line() +   labs(     title = "Estimated count as a function of x2",     y = "Estimated count"   )  # pointwise normal intervals from the delta method y_delta <- response_derivatives(m, data = ds, focal = "x2",   type = "central", uncertainty = "delta")  # draw response derivatives p2 <- y_d |>   ggplot(aes(x = x2, y = .derivative)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = .lower_ci, ymax = .upper_ci), alpha = 0.2) +   geom_line() +   labs(     title = "Estimated 1st derivative of estimated count",     y = "First derivative"   )  # draw both panels p1 + p2 + plot_layout(nrow = 2)

title: gratia (development version)
text: gratia new neon hex logo. pkgdown site uses pink g logo favicon. Breaking change: Parametric plots now use covariates evaluated model default: log(x) plotted log(x), matching axis label. Use back_transform = TRUE plot original covariates. option available draw.gam(), assemble.gam(), draw.parametric_effects() draw.smooth_estimates(), including interaction axes, tensor products, rugs conditioning facets (#412). Multi-column basis expansions retain original covariate axes. Changing coordinate scale change estimated effects intervals. transform argument parametric_effects() deprecated. Replace back_transform = !transform (#412). Breaking change: draw.gam() assemble.gam() now default parametric = NULL, including parametric terms alongside smooths select = NULL. Selecting smooths explicitly continues draw smooths, unless parametric = TRUE supplied. Use parametric = FALSE restore previous default. Additional panels can change plot layouts length plot lists returned assemble() draw(wrap = FALSE). Parametric effect intervals now include intercept uncertainty default, including covariance intercept term. Partial estimates unchanged. Use overall_uncertainty = FALSE parametric_effects(), draw() assemble() recover term-intervals. term uses intercept linear predictor; models without intercept unaffected. Surface plotting related evaluation functions now accept n_2d, default 50 points along surface axis (#153). Default surface grids therefore shrink 10,000 2,500 points per panel. Curve conditioning slice resolutions can controlled separately. Derivative functions now choose finite-difference step automatically eps = NULL, using fitted covariate range, derivative order difference method. reduces rounding error second derivatives. Supply positive eps specify absolute step size. appraise() now automatically uses scalable plots least 10,000 observations used fitting. Set scalable = TRUE FALSE override behaviour, change scalable_threshold. Explicit xlab = NULL ylab = NULL now request default axis labels continuous-covariate fs plots random-effect tensor curves, consistent univariate smooths. Previously, explicit NULL suppressed labels (#308). Tweedie cumulative distribution functions now use fast Poisson-Gamma mixtures 1 < p < 2 instead requiring tweedie package (#410). Gamma case (p = 2) uses native R distribution functions. Mixture calculations warn return available approximations work accuracy limits reached. tweedie package now optional, Suggests, needed numerical inversion requested fallback = TRUE. posterior_samples() now uses separate random-number streams coefficient response draws. Response draws given seed differ earlier releases, remain reproducible. gratia now requires mgcv >= 1.9-4 R >= 4.4.0. glmmTMB support now requires released version 1.1.15.2 later, development version glmmTMB longer needed.

title: gratia (development version)
text: New site articles explain model diagnostics, grouped surveys, glmmTMB sdmTMB models, prediction comparisons, response distributions, smooth effects different spatial domains. include fitted examples explain assumptions behind estimates, intervals checks. Residual diagnostics posterior predictive checks now cover lm, glm, gam/bam, gamm/gamm4, glmmTMB, univariate GJRM sdmTMB models using fitted response distributions. Probability integral transform (PIT) residuals map observations fitted probabilities, randomising probability mass discrete responses. Quantile residuals convert probabilities standard-normal scores. See ?diagnostic_support supported families, conditioning choices limitations. Prepared diagnostic objects carry selected conditioning sdmTMB field choices residual plotting methods. Mixed-model diagnostics can hold fitted random effects fixed average fitted distribution. Joint response simulations use fitting packages’ generators retain temporal spatial covariance shared random effects. Marginal residuals can use means, variances ranks simulations. Direct nlme::lme() lme4::merMod fits also support residual posterior predictive checks. Non-Gaussian gamm fits estimated penalized quasi-likelihood (PQL) support approximate checks residual working correlation. nlme calculations retain covariance random effects block designs, fitted factor contrasts observation order subsetting missing-value removal. sdmTMB residual diagnostics now offer four ways treat random fields: draw fitted fields approximate posterior hold fixed (field_method = "mle-mvn", default), hold field estimates fixed (field_method = "mle-eb"), average fitted-field uncertainty (field_method = "mle-mvn-integrated"), simulate new fields (conditioning = "marginal"). Plot labels identify choice. Posterior predictive checks separately include approximate parameter uncertainty. See ?diagnostic_support checks assess limitations.
